builder_plan.scenario: Your self-hosted model spends too long generating answers token by token.
builder_plan.change: Check whether a compatible draft model and serving integration exist before renting compute.
builder_plan.baseline: The same target with speculation off, then your existing drafter if you have one.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted draft length, tokens per second, tail latency, output quality, and total GPU cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Long-Context Drafting Does Not Require Long-Context Drafters
summary: Replaces training or fine-tuning a long-context drafter (or shipping a multi-token head) by reusing released short-context drafters with two inference-time mechanisms: bounding the drafter's attention cache and re-basing rotary indices into the trained range, implemented as one vLLM-side configuration. No weights are modified, the single tunable saturates early, and drafter compute cost becomes constant rather than growing with context. Adoption fails if the speculative cost per emitted token exceeds matched target-only cost, if either mechanism is removed, or when no compatible released drafter exists for the target model.
rationale: It is a weight-free, vLLM-side configuration that preserves existing speculative decoding speedups at long context, fitting constrained single-GPU or API-based production stacks.
technique: Frozen short-context drafters for long-context speculative decoding

claims.statement: Replaces training or fine-tuning a long-context drafter (or shipping a multi-token head) by reusing released short-context drafters with two inference-time mechanisms: bounding the drafter's attention cache and re-basing rotary indices into the trained range, implemented as one vLLM-side configuration. No weights are modified, the single tunable saturates early, and drafter compute cost becomes constant rather than growing with context. Adoption fails if the speculative cost per emitted token exceeds matched target-only cost, if either mechanism is removed, or when no compatible released drafter exists for the target model.

A frozen short-context drafter retains its short-context speculative speedup out to two million tokens across three target-drafter pairs and five corpora, costing at most 0.16x of the short-length speedup; the claim is flatness of speedup over context length, not a new multiple.
